prompt: Vault issues a unique database credential for each service instance with a one-hour lease. Assuming revocation succeeds and the database enforces it for the relevant access, what benefit does this provide after one credential is stolen?

options.text: The attacker has permanent access, because database users can't be removed automatically
options.explanation: Vault revokes (drops) the user when the lease expires or is revoked; that is the whole point of dynamic secrets.

options.text: Successful expiry or revocation limits credential reuse, and auditing can identify the distinct credential issued to the instance
options.explanation: Correct under the stated enforcement assumptions. Distinct credentials narrow exposure and attribute activity to the credential, though not conclusively to the original instance after theft.

options.text: All instances must be restarted, because they share the same credential
options.explanation: With dynamic secrets they do not share a credential, so revoking one doesn't affect the rest.

options.text: Dynamic secrets prevent the theft in the first place
options.explanation: They don't prevent theft; they shrink the value and lifetime of what is stolen.

workedExample: A unique leased credential narrows which principal must be revoked. Expiry or an explicit revoke request triggers configured database revocation; connectivity, permissions and existing-session behavior must be checked. Audit logs can associate operations with the credential, but an attacker using it impersonates the same principal. Monitor failed revocations rather than assuming immediate deletion.
